direction: Symplectic-first design: build all components around energy conservation guarantees
rationale: Energy conservation is the primary quality metric; choosing symplectic integrators from the start ensures bounded energy error and enables meaningful benchmarking
first_step: Implement leapfrog integrator before any non-symplectic method
expected_signal: Energy drift < 0.1% over 100 orbits in Kepler validation

direction: Vectorized numpy brute-force as the accuracy baseline before tree codes
rationale: Direct summation provides exact (within softening) forces that serve as ground truth for Barnes-Hut accuracy testing
first_step: Implement fully vectorized O(N^2) force computation using numpy broadcasting
expected_signal: Force symmetry F_ij = -F_ji verified to machine precision

direction: Benchmark-driven development: implement test problems before optimization
rationale: Having Kepler, figure-eight, and Plummer benchmarks established early enables regression testing as algorithms are optimized
first_step: Create initial condition generators alongside the first integrator
expected_signal: All benchmark scenarios reproducible with seed=42
